clips.label: v3-0
clips.text: Sorry I kept you waiting. That's AI chips every day waiting for data. And you, Sky, you pay full price to wait.

clips.label: v3-1
clips.text: So first, why change?

clips.label: v3-2
clips.text: Ofcom says traditional TV fell by twelve percent in a year as people move to streaming.

clips.label: v3-3
clips.text: Netflix and YouTube already know what you want to watch, so Sky needs that too, and fast.

clips.label: v3-4
clips.text: Second, why now?

clips.label: v3-5
clips.text: Well, you've already started with Sky Q voice search.

clips.label: v3-6
clips.text: Now, the next step is an AI assistant that knows each household.

clips.label: v3-7
clips.text: Imagine asking, Sky, make me scared.

clips.label: v3-8
clips.text: Third, why DDN?

clips.label: v3-9
clips.text: Idle chips will still cost you, and Cast AI found that enterprise chips average around five percent of use.

clips.label: v3-10
clips.text: It's like paying for a whole Sky Sports bundle just to watch Arsenal lose.

clips.label: v3-11
clips.text: Now DDN's Infinia keeps data flowing to the chips.

clips.label: v3-12
clips.text: And they say customers reach up to ninety nine percent busy and cut costs per token by seventy five percent.

clips.label: v3-13
clips.text: Plus, they already work with media companies like Canal Plus and Starz.

clips.label: v3-14
clips.text: So the ask is clear.

clips.label: v3-15
clips.text: Let DDN run a pilot on the AI behind your voice search or your next assistant.

clips.label: v3-16
clips.text: Then measure the values before and after.

clips.label: v4-ins
clips.text: And if both improve, scale it.

clips.label: v3-17
clips.text: So Sky.

clips.label: v3-18
clips.text: Don't be the next Blockbuster.

clips.label: v3-19
clips.text: Thank you.
